operational_simulations: small hotel staffing and housekeeping allocation under volatile arrivals and cancellations
destination disruption recovery for weather, transport interruption, and event-driven demand shifts
small-property maintenance, guest-request, and back-office workload planning under reduced staffing
deterministic_and_statistical_baselines: PMS booking curves and occupancy forecast
minimum staffing rules and skill constraints
priority queues, shift templates, and manual manager overrides
statistical demand forecasting feeding deterministic scheduling or optimization

training_data.input_data: booking curve, cancellations, arrivals, departures, room status, events, weather, staffing availability, skills, tasks, maintenance and guest requests available at planning time
training_data.target_or_reward: realized workload, service delay, overtime, room turnaround, unmet demand and constrained operating cost
training_data.label_source: PMS, workforce, housekeeping, maintenance and guest-service outcomes; availability and consistency are unknown
training_data.prediction_time: before daily or shift-level staffing and task allocation
training_data.expected_volume: unknown; likely limited for individual small properties and more viable across multi-property groups
training_data.class_balance: not applicable for continuous demand targets; disruption and severe service-failure events are expected to be rare
training_data.historical_coverage: unknown; requires synchronized booking, task, staffing and outcome history across seasonality and disruptions
training_data.train_validation_split: time-based split with holdout seasons, properties and disruption periods
training_data.leakage_risks: using final occupancy, same-day task completions, overtime, complaints, revised staffing or disruption outcomes unavailable at planning time
training_data.representativeness_risks: property size, destination, season, service model, labor practice, channel mix and exceptional events vary materially
training_data.feedback_loop: manager overrides and realized service outcomes should be retained separately from model recommendations
training_data.privacy_and_usage_constraints: minimize guest and worker personal data; avoid employee surveillance or automated employment decisions
training_data.fallback_if_data_is_insufficient: booking-curve statistics, configured workload ratios, constraint-based scheduling and manager approval

existing_landscape.summary: Current hotel operations and revenue-management platforms already combine demand forecasting, staffing, housekeeping, task prioritization and constrained operational planning. A new case would duplicate HOSP-001 or represent a product configuration rather than a differentiated opportunity.

notes: No opportunity published. Forecasting and constrained scheduling are technically plausible, but the operational outcome overlaps HOSP-001 and mature hotel operations/revenue-management products. The main remaining work for small properties is data integration, configuration and adoption rather than a distinct intelligent architecture.
